items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I was very big fan of Joe Morello’s... I used to do small little pockets of tributes to Joe Morello

ctx.x: Who were some of the influential drummers that you listened to that you liked at that time?

Well my first big influence was Gene Krupa. He was like the biggest influence on me. Right at the beginning I was a huge fan of Gene’s. I loved everything about him. I loved his style and his sound, and his flair, his showmanship, and the way he would really put over a great drum solo — even add that little extra pizzazz that just made me say “Wow.” Because a lot of times you see some wonderful musicians and they just look like they can’t wait for the next taxi out of town. They’re not enjoying themselves or…
From that list it’s almost as if you went backwards in first listening to like Krupa and then listening to guys that came even before him.

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: It’s like Joe Morello told me one time

ctx.x: Yeah. What do you tell your, with jazz majors, what do you advise to them as far as post- graduation and making a living?

Swing or I’ll kill you. No, no, it’s just old jokes, sorry. Old musicians will remember that old joke. It’s like Joe Morello told me one time, he said, “A lot of times you can’t remember how many bars there are to a tune, but the old musicians can remember how many tunes there are to a bar” and I left my cowbell down on the campus, God-dog it.
